## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Single-anonymized (single-blind): reviewers know author identity, authors do not know reviewer identity. Minimum two review reports per manuscript that proceeds to review; reviewers given 7-10 days (extensions common). Preceded by a two-stage pre-check (Editorial Office technical/ethics pre-check + Academic Editor editorial pre-check). |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | *(pending)* |

> Source: https://www.mdpi.com/journal/jemr/instructions

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | JEMR follows MDPI's standard publisher-wide GenAI policy since moving from Bern Open Publishing to MDPI (Vol. 18, Jan 2025). GenAI/LLM tools cannot be listed as authors (do not meet authorship criteria). Where GenAI was used for text/data/graphics generation, study design, or data analysis/interpretation, authors must add a disclosure statement naming the tool, version, and purpose in the Acknowledgments section, and take full responsibility for the content. No outright ban and no journal-specific customization found beyond MDPI's boilerplate policy replicated verbatim on the JEMR instructions page. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.mdpi.com/journal/jemr/instructions |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Yes. JEMR accepts submissions previously posted as preprints, provided they have not undergone peer review elsewhere. MDPI operates its own Preprints.org server; posting there does not affect peer review.
> Source: https://www.mdpi.com/journal/jemr/instructions

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Original research articles, reviews (incl. systematic reviews per PRISMA), short communications, and case reports on all aspects of oculomotor functioning: eye-recording methodology, neurophysiological/cognitive models, attention, reading, and applications in neurology, ergonomics, media research, HCI, education, driving, consumer/neuromarketing research. Active 2026 special issue signals strong current interest in AI-enhanced eye-tracking (machine learning, computer vision, multimodal modeling incl. EEG fusion, predictive gaze modeling) - deadline 20 Nov 2026, guest-edited by Hedda Martina Sola (neuromarketing) and Jasenka Gajdos Kljusuric (applied modeling/AI tools).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** eye-tracking methodology / recording techniques, machine learning & computer vision applied to gaze data, multimodal integration (eye-tracking + EEG or other neurophysiological measures), predictive/generative gaze modeling, attention and reading research, systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA), applied/consumer neuroscience and neuromarketing studies, case reports on oculomotor conditions

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**Sources cited across this entry:**
- https://scirev.org/journal/journal-of-eye-movement-research/ (only n=1 review, editor-provided stats fields all 'n/a'; that single review reports a 2.4-week first round and 'managed via email instead of a publication system' - this describes the pre-2025 Bern Open Publishing workflow, NOT the current MDPI/SuSy system, so it is stale and not reported as a current fact)
- https://www.mdpi.com/journal/jemr/about (aims & scope)
- https://www.mdpi.com/journal/jemr/instructions
- https://www.mdpi.com/journal/jemr/special_issues/7NX3D3I604 (active AI special issue CFP, deadline 2026-11-20)

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why:**
- **experiential.review_time_months**: SciRev has only a single review (n=1) and that review predates the Jan-2025 MDPI takeover (describes an email-based workflow inconsistent with MDPI's SuSy platform), so it cannot be treated as representative of the current journal. No other first-hand timing report found.
- **experiential.desk_reject_pct**: No SciRev aggregate stats (editor did not supply percent-accepted/percent-rejected), no forum-reported figure found in English or Chinese sources.
- **experiential.acceptance_note**: No multi-report pattern; the sole SciRev entry is a single anecdote, not a pattern, and is likely pre-MDPI.
- **experiential.reviewer_culture**: Zero hits on muchong.com, zhihu, fabiaoji, and Reddit r/AskAcademia specifically discussing JEMR review experience or reviewer behavior - searches returned unrelated ophthalmology-journal content or no results at all.
- **ai_policy.gate (journal-specific customization)**: No JEMR-specific AI policy page exists distinct from MDPI's publisher-wide boilerplate; cannot confirm whether editors apply any stricter/looser practice in reality (e.g., via desk-reject patterns) due to lack of experiential data.
